endpoint_measured: Per-sample keydown, EventDispatch, Paint/DrawFrame, compositor submit, swap/present, and any available displayed-frame timestamp from the same browser trace configuration.
required_controls: Run the same 990ms, 1000ms, and 1300ms key-held rows and matching complete-keypress rows, with browser revision, trace categories, refresh rate, and retained-sample IDs recorded.
success_gate: The externally presented-frame endpoint preserves the key-held 1000ms drop direction while complete-keypress rows stay flat; the added compositor/display tail is reported separately from EventDispatch.
failure_interpretation: If presentation timestamps flatten the 1000ms key-held drop, the current claim remains limited to Chromium internal visual endpoints, not presented frames.
claim_boundary: Needed only before claiming compositor/display presentation timing.

endpoint_measured: First frame in which an OCR, template-match, or image-recognition pass recognizes the newly inserted glyph in a crop anchored to the DOM Range or textbox target box.
required_controls: Use the same retained samples as the screenshot-pixel probe, require target-box and typed-range overlap, and preserve the 990ms/1000ms/1300ms key-held plus complete-keypress controls.
success_gate: Recognized-glyph timing keeps the key-held 1000ms drop and agrees in ordering with localized changed-pixel timing within the declared recognition tolerance.
failure_interpretation: If recognition disagrees with localized changed pixels, treat the current screenshot result as a pixel-localization result, not semantic first-visible-glyph proof.
claim_boundary: Needed only before claiming semantic first-visible-glyph timing.

endpoint_measured: Visual endpoint rows with and without trace screenshots, heavy render categories, and the external calibration instrumentation enabled.
required_controls: Pair each observer-on row with an observer-off or lighter-observer row at the same delay/mode and compare p50 ordering, retained counts, and first-key behavior.
success_gate: The 1000ms key-held drop persists without relying on the observer that supplies the endpoint, and observer-on overhead is reported as a separate offset.
failure_interpretation: If the observer creates or erases the drop, keep the result as instrumentation-specific and do not generalize it to user-visible timing.
claim_boundary: Required before using trace screenshots or external capture as causal evidence.

endpoint_measured: Camera-visible glyph or display transition timestamp aligned to keydown or a visual trigger, with camera fps, shutter/exposure, display refresh rate, and panel mode recorded.
required_controls: Use the same delay/mode rows plus a calibration flash or equivalent alignment marker; keep browser trace IDs when possible so camera-visible frames can be joined to EventDispatch and internal visual endpoints.
success_gate: Camera-visible glyph timing preserves the key-held 1000ms drop direction and gives a stable additive display tail relative to compositor/presented-frame timing.
failure_interpretation: If camera timing is too noisy or disagrees with compositor traces, report hardware/display timing as unresolved and keep CI claims internal.
claim_boundary: Needed only before claiming hardware-to-eye timing.

endpoint_measured: Joined per-sample table covering keydown, EventDispatch, RAF, Paint/DrawFrame, changed screenshot, localized pixels, presented frame if available, recognized glyph if available, and camera-visible glyph if used.
required_controls: Retain the CI p50 discard/window rules, the same input-mode controls, and the same per-sample source IDs so endpoint movement can be decomposed rather than compared across unrelated samples.
success_gate: The external endpoint confirms the same qualitative shape as the internal endpoint stack and any extra tail is smaller than, or clearly separable from, the EventDispatch-driven drop.
failure_interpretation: If the joined endpoint stack changes the qualitative conclusion, narrow the report wording to the deepest endpoint that passed and keep the disagreement as the next open question.
claim_boundary: Defines when the report may widen beyond Chromium internal visual propagation.
